newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong passes controversial state-secrets law.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong passes controversial state-secrets law.

text.p: Hong Kong has enacted a controversial anti-espionage law in line with an Anglo-Chinese agreement on the territory's July 1 return to China.
The Legislative Council passed the Official Secrets Bill, aimed against theft of state secrets, on Wednesday night.

It was earlier agreed by Britain and China in diplomatic negotiations on the sovereignty transfer. The bill localises Britain's stringent Official Secrets Act to ensure Hong Kong has a law to tackle espionage and security threats after the handover.
Pro-democracy politicians attacked the measure in the legislature as a curb on the free flow of information.
Hong Kong, at the southern tip of communist-ruled China, was once seen as a vital listening and observation post for spies on Beijing.
Offences outlined by the bill include actions such as approaching a "prohibited place" for "a purpose prejudical to the safety interests of the United Kingdom or Hong Kong".
After the handover, the reference to the United Kingdom will be deleted and replaced by China.

China has promised the territory of 6.4 million it will keep its way of life unchanged for 50 years, but many in Hong Kong have interpreted Chinese moves to water down democracy and civil rights as an omen of impending repression.
Anxiety rose recently when future Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa unveiled plans inspired by China to curb a right to protest and foreign funding of political groups.
